Pricing is quote-oriented and should not look like an e-commerce checkout module.

heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 (Image Generation) and Seedance 1.5 Pro (Video Generation) — advanced foundation models developed by ByteDance for high-quality visual content creation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a full-bleed editorial hero with a warm orange mesh gradient, subtle grid lines, and precision-line motifs to create a premium enterprise feel. Keep the left side text-forward for clarity, but make the overall composition asymmetrical with floating chips and layered product callouts on the right, avoiding a standard split layout. Treat the hero as a polished campaign poster rather than a generic SaaS banner; no autoplay video in the hero, just a refined visual system that implies motion through overlays, depth, and staggered entrance animation.

repetitionBreakers: Hero uses split editorial contrast; trust uses a dark marquee band; products shift to alternating spotlight-plus-grid tabs; pricing uses a centered comparison card; testimonials switch to a carousel; form returns to a high-focus compact card.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro by ByteDance | AI Images & Videos for Creative Teams
blueprint.metaDescription: Create high-quality AI images and videos with ByteDance’s Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Built for creative directors, video producers, and enterprise teams who need precise, high-fidelity visual content.

sections.backgroundTreatment: full-bleed brand-orange with thin precision-line overlays and subtle layered media framing
sections.designNote: Dynamic above-the-fold split hero with the headline answering what this is, the subheadline clarifying it is for creative professionals and enterprises, and a single solid accent CTA labeled 'Get started'. Use a layered collage on the right: abstract AI visual frames, product mockups, and floating pills for Seedream 4.5, Seedance 1.5 Pro, 4K output, Audio-visual sync, and Multimodal creation. Keep the hero content-first but visually rich so it feels premium and enterprise-confident.

Immediate trust layer in a dark marquee band with 3-6 recognisable logos. Since logos are the required proof type, make this a prominent confidence strip directly after the hero. Use a continuous marquee to maximize recognition and signal enterprise readiness without adding extra copy.

Two distinct product blocks with alternating layouts and different visual energy. First spotlight Seedream 4.5 as the lead click-driver with a tabbed feature system and preview panel for image generation, editing, composition, and typographic rendering. Then switch background and layout rhythm for Seedance 1.5 Pro with a more cinematic but still editorial preview, emphasizing audio-video generation, lip-sync, camera control, and speed. This section should feel modular rather than generic SaaS, with one block more technical and one more expressive.

Use this as a trust-and-clarity bridge rather than a generic benefits dump. Present concise enterprise-oriented reasons to choose the platform in a clean icon-card grid, focusing on buying confidence, implementation ease, and support. Keep it lighter and more factual than the product sections so it resets the rhythm.

A focused pricing comparison area with two product cards, using the provided pricing data and a clear primary action on each card labeled 'Get started'. Keep it more utilitarian than emotional. Since ctaAggression is not soft, this section should still be conversion-oriented, but the hero and product sections remain the main narrative drivers.

Use a carousel because there are 4+ testimonials. Make this a dark credibility section to create strong visual contrast after the white pricing area. Rotate quotes from creative director, video producer, art director, and marketing manager to reinforce both image and video use cases. Keep typography large, confident, and editorial.

Final conversion section should be a compact centered card with minimal fields and a single full-width mobile CTA labeled 'Get started'. The tone should feel assured and friction-light, not pushy. Use a floating card with soft shadow and precise spacing so the CTA lands after credibility has been established.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long, so it needs the smaller 16+ word treatment to preserve hierarchy and avoid awkward wrapping.

colours.colourReason: The brand palette already defines the identity: orange as the core action/energy color, white for clarity, and deep charcoal for text and contrast. This keeps the page unmistakably Techjockey while avoiding any unsupported generic gradient system.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-screen dark/ink-toned split hero with brand mark at top, large headline, short supporting paragraph, and a compact benefit list beneath. Text is left-aligned and stacked for quick scanning, with strong contrast and minimal visual clutter.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Hero first, then a lead form section immediately below. Content progression is linear and conversion-focused, with limited narrative expansion and no visible multi-step storytelling.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple functional card container with solid background, subtle border or shadow, rounded corners, and dense form/content grouping. Visual emphasis comes from hierarchy rather than decoration.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary conversion CTA appears in the hero and again in product-specific sections. CTAs are action-oriented, short, and repeated at decision points rather than using a sticky or persistent bar.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing module is present in the reference structure; the pattern is lead-generation oriented instead of price-comparison oriented.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer is not visible in the provided reference HTML; no reusable footer pattern can be inferred.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Brand/logo image in the hero with no dominant product imagery. Media usage is minimal and supporting, not immersive; the layout relies primarily on typography and lists.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Modular feature sections with label, headline, descriptive paragraph, and bullet-style capability lists. Sections are suitable for stacked product modules, with progressive disclosure through separate feature blocks rather than tabs or accordions.
referenceMap.formPattern: Prominent lead form card placed near the top after the hero. The form uses hidden tracking inputs, suggesting a conversion-optimized capture pattern with minimal visible fields and backend instrumentation.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, non-animated presentation with no evident motion system; if any motion exists, it is not represented in the HTML structure.
designNotes: Conversion-first page structure with immediate form access.
Typography and hierarchy do most of the visual work.
Best suited to enterprise products that need fast explanation and lead capture.
Use short, scannable bullets for proof points and capabilities.
Keep media light unless a specific product demo is required.

mustHaveMoments: Above-the-fold hero with a concise value proposition and primary CTA
Dominant customer/logo trust strip near the top
Gallery section featuring AI-generated images and videos
Dedicated product sections for Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro
Pricing / quote cards for both solutions
Testimonial block with role-based enterprise credibility
Final CTA section reinforcing demo or quote request
avoidPatterns: Overly decorative or immersive hero that weakens clarity
Long-form storytelling before the offer is understood
Heavy multi-step funnel or excessive form fields
Price-led comparison framing that distracts from lead capture
Generic stock-style visuals without real AI output examples
Badge-only trust strategy without visible logos
Sticky or overly persistent CTAs that feel pushy
designStrategy.reasoning: This page should behave like a high-intent enterprise lead-generation asset for two closely related AI products. The audience is professional and solution-aware, so the structure should quickly explain capability, show proof, and convert into a demo or quote request. Because the brief says visitors trust logos most, the trust layer should prioritize logo visibility over badges or statistics. A split hero is the best fit: it preserves clarity, supports quick scanning, and allows a compact proof area or product preview alongside the core message. Since the input specifically asks for a gallery section containing videos and images, visual proof must be an explicit mid-page moment to demonstrate output quality and reduce abstraction. The overall tone should feel confident and premium rather than playful, with balanced spacing and moderately strong CTAs repeated at key decision points.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
